threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the 48 bus pulls up late, like it's some betrayal. All the locals just roll their eyes and check their phones.
Saw a guy on the 35 last night bickering with a pigeon like it was his long-lost mate. Only in Brixton, right? The pigeon seemed unbothered.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the corner Kebab shop started knowing my order by heart, and the old lady at the bakery always had my favorite Brötchen set aside.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice the U-Bahn stops at a complete standstill during a Streik? Everyone just pulls out snacks and starts chilling, like it's a picnic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the BART delays are just an invitation to grab a taco at Taqueria La Cumbre instead of stressing over the schedule.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 down on Market when it stopped mid-ride for a random karaoke session. Guy in a hoodie belted out ‘Livin' on a Prayer.’ Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just for Gaudí and cafés, but they miss the Sunday afternoon potlucks at local plazas that truly bring the community together.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a new arrival by their hesitance to order the local tapas like patatas bravas—most get lost trying to pronounce it.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still take a cab when it rains instead of just popping into the nearest pub for a pint and waiting it out.
Riding the 333 last night, the driver stopped mid-route for a spontaneous sing-along with a group of students. Brixton's nights never fail to surprise.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler on a scooter, expertly weaving through a crowd outside Café Savigny while the street musicians played a melancholic tune.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can see a hipster on a bike juggling while waiting for the tram. Only in Kreuzberg would that be a daily commute spectacle.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they skip the BART to Civic Center and know the quickest bus route instead, even if it’s the most delayed one.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 this morning, and a guy was singing ‘I’m Still Standing’—talk about a soundtrack for a crowded commute. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. But the real charm lies in hidden plazas where locals sip vermut and chat, far from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered expressions while trying to decode the metro map at Fontana station.
